provisional_canonical_claim: Let M be an o-minimal expansion of a dense linear order and let f be a definable unary function on an interval. The domain admits a finite partition into points and intervals such that on every interval piece f is continuous and is either constant or strictly monotone.
domain_and_universes: Provisionally, a first-order language L expanding the language of a dense linear order, a nonempty carrier M with an L-structure and compatible dense linear order, parameters allowed exactly as in the selected source, an interval domain, and a unary definable function. Universes and the expansion interface remain open.
quantifiers: parameter set or tuple, subject to the source convention
hypotheses: the order on M is dense, linear, and without endpoints if required by the selected source
the L-structure is o-minimal: every definable unary subset is a finite union of points and intervals
the graph and domain of f are definable under the selected parameter convention
conclusion: Provisionally, a finite partition of the domain into point and interval pieces on which f is continuous and constant or strictly monotone; exact endpoint and direction conventions remain open.

alternate_encodings.target: a finite exceptional set whose complementary interval components each carry one continuity/monotonicity behavior
alternate_encodings.relationship: intended equivalent to an explicit finite cell partition after checked transport

alternate_encodings.target: the defining one-dimensional finite-union-of-points-and-intervals property alone
alternate_encodings.relationship: definition/premise only, not a substitute for the provisional monotonicity conclusion

excluded_degenerate_cases: The statement phase must decide empty domains, singleton intervals, unbounded intervals, endpoint inclusion, partial versus total functions, named parameters, and whether discontinuity points are isolated separately. No convention may be silently chosen.
foundation_profile: Lean 4 dependent type theory; classical logic and choice requirements of finite decomposition and definability remain to be audited
tcb_profile: Lean kernel 4.29.0 and pinned mathlib are candidate components; exact imports, declaration, dependency closure, and axiom profile remain open
computation_profile: noncomputable finite-partition existence theorem expected; no oracle, experiment, or unchecked certificate is credited
freshness_and_revocation_policy: Invalidate on source selection, canonical wording, parameter convention, o-minimality encoding, Lean target, toolchain, mathlib pin, assurance profile, or validator change; independent review and review due date remain open.
status_boundary: Self-tested planned intake only. The repository wording is too broad to freeze an exact theorem without primary-source review. There is no canonical Lean target, H0, obligation registry, proof credit, accepted task state, audit completion, or theorem completion.
